questions.question: State the three ingredients needed for a mid-latitude cyclone to develop on the polar front, and give the direction of circulation around the low in the Southern Hemisphere.
questions.expected_answer: A sharp temperature contrast across the polar front, where cold polar air meets warm subtropical air; rotation supplied by the Coriolis force, which deflects moving air to its left in the Southern Hemisphere; and upper-air divergence, where the jet stream drags air away from the top of the system so that surface pressure falls and more air spirals inward. The circulation around the low is clockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.

questions.question: Describe the three stages in the life cycle of a mid-latitude cyclone, and explain why occlusion leads to the death of the system.
questions.expected_answer: Initial or wave stage: air masses shearing past each other kink the polar front into a shallow wave with falling pressure at its tip. Mature stage: the wave opens into a deep low with a gentle leading warm front, a steep trailing cold front, and a warm sector of warm humid air between them. Occlusion stage: the faster cold front catches the warm front and lifts the warm sector completely off the surface. Cut off from its supply of warm surface air, the temperature contrast collapses and the system weakens and dissipates.

questions.question: Narrate the weather experienced in a south-coast town such as George before, during and after the passage of a cold front, referring to temperature, pressure, wind and sky.
questions.expected_answer: Before: warm, humid conditions in the warm sector, north-westerly wind, steadily falling pressure, and cloud building over the sea to the west. During: cumulonimbus with heavy cold showers and possible thunder, snow on the high peaks, and the wind swinging from north-west through west to south-west — the signature of the passage. After: temperature six to ten degrees lower, pressure rising as the South Atlantic High ridges in, cold gusty south-westerly wind, and clearing skies with bright cold sunshine between showers.
